newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel diamond exports fell 5 pct in December.
newsitem.headline: Israel diamond exports fell 5 pct in December.

text.p: Israel's net exports of polished diamonds fell five percent in December from a year earlier to $232 million, the Industry and Trade Ministry said on Wednesday.
For all of 1996, net diamond exports were up four percent to $4.0 billion from $3.845 billion in 1995.

Tsafrir Anbar, the head of the diamond unit at the ministry, said the full-year figure marked a record high. However, he noted that exports fell in November and December and that there was a worrying increase in returns in the last month of the year.

Anbar said the sharp rise in exports of partially cut diamonds indicated continued strong worldwide demand for partially worked stones from Israel. Exports in this category rose 22 percent last year to $837 million.
He noted an increase in the quality and price of stones polished in Israel and a continued decline in the polishing of cheaper, smaller diamonds because of high local production costs.
Israel's principal markets for polished diamonds last year were the United States (43.4 percent of total exports), Japan (16.8 percent) and Hong Kong (16.7 percent).
The aggregate debt of the Israeli diamond industry to banks rose 17 percent in the year to $958 million.
